description: Restructures a rough presentation/talk/deck outline around a real narrative arc (setup, tension, resolution) instead of rewording the same bullets onto slides in the same order. Finds the throughline the material resolves and flags problems by name — a buried lede (key point mid-deck, not near the front), no throughline connecting sections, a data-heavy section dropped into a story flow with no transition, or a conclusion that summarizes instead of resolving the opening's tension. Use when someone hands over a rough bullet outline, agenda, or slide list and asks to find the story in it, fix the pacing, explain why a deck "falls flat," reorder sections, or state the throughline — even without the word "narrative." Also covers "does this deck's order make sense," "the ending feels weak," "too much setup before the point," "what's my through-line." Leaves a well-paced outline alone rather than forcing an unneeded reshuffle. Not for line-editing copy, visual design, speaker notes, or screenplay structure.
